# Kana Derivation Chart

> An interactive chart of how the Japanese hiragana and katakana syllabaries were each derived from kanji. The whole site is one page.

The chart lays out the basic kana in the traditional gojūon grid (consonant by vowel). Selecting a cell shows the cursive simplification behind its hiragana form and the component extraction behind its katakana form, each traced back to its source kanji, with the romanization. A second tab covers the voiced and semi-voiced (dakuten and handakuten) variants, and short notes flag archaic kana and duplicate readings. The chart is rendered in the browser with JavaScript; there is no API and no other page.

## Pages

- [Kana Derivation Chart](https://kana.gfrm.in/): the chart itself, with hiragana, katakana, source kanji and romanization for each kana
